- When sentiment is strongly bullish (≥1.0) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly to avoid overshoot.
- When sentiment is bearish (≤-1.0) in recent days, model often underestimates; adjust upward slightly to capture mean reversion or rebound.
- After a sharp price spike, model frequently overcorrects downward; delay or reduce the magnitude of subsequent downward moves.
- Model tends to lag in mean reversion — especially when sentiment shifts from bullish to neutral/bearish — so anticipate a slower correction than true outcome.
- For 30-day forecasts, model often overestimates early in the horizon (first 5–10 days) when sentiment is volatile; cap early forecast peaks to avoid overconfidence.
- When sentiment is mixed or neutral, model often fails to capture volatility; use sentiment as a filter to dampen forecast variance in low-signal periods.
